text.p: Italian BTP bond futures held to higher levels in late afternoon boosted by weaker than expected U.S. inflation data and greater confidence in Europe's economic and monetary union getting underway as planned, dealers said.

Futures had a volatile day opening higher then shedding gains to slip into negative territory before support came from U.S. data which showed producer prices down for the fifth straight month in May, thus easing fears of a U.S. rate rise.
"This was a rather uncertain trading day until the U.S. figures gave BPTs, bunds and most other world bonds a boost in the afternoon," said one trader on the LIFFE market.

Dealers said that the U.S. data pointed towards a healthy economy showing high growth, low unemployment and low inflation. This all pointed to an easing of the odds that the Federal Reserve would raise U.S. interest rates in July.
On the domestic side, higher than expected Italian April industrial output gave the market early support, but futures soon ran into profit taking as the mood shifted in late morning.

Attention through the day was on the Franco-German meeting in Poitiers, and French President Jacques Chira's appeal for everything to be done to ensure that EMU should start on time helped settle European bond markets.
In late trading, the September LIFFE BTP futures contract showed gains of 13 basis points to 131.76.
